title: The Habit Loop: Cue, Routine, Reward
t: The Habit Loop: Cue, Routine, Reward
description: The loop (Duhigg’s; the Power of Habit) — the neurology — cycles: the cue (the triggered — the time, the place, the emotion, the people, the preceding action), the routine (the behavior — the physical, the mental, the emotional), and the reward (the craved — the satisfied; the remembered). The craving (the anticipated — the driving). The engineering: the identified (the loop — the diagnosed), the kept (the cue and reward — the same), and the swapped (the routine — the new). The principle: the looped behavior automatic — the cued, the routined, the rewarded; the changed by swapping routine.
key_points: Cue triggers; routine runs; reward satisfies
Change by keeping cue/reward, swapping routine
how_it_works: Identify cue-routine-reward, keep cue and reward, insert new routine.

title: Atomic Habits: The Four Laws
description: The four laws (Clear’s) — the behavior design — state: the obvious (the 1st — the cue; the make it), the attractive (the 2nd — the craving; the make it), the easy (the 3rd — the response; the make it), and the satisfying (the 4th — the reward; the make it). The inversions (the breaking — the make it invisible, unattractive, hard, unsatisfying). The compounding (the 1% — the aggregated; the plateau of latent potential). The principle: the lawed habits built — the obvious, the attractive, the easy, the satisfying; the inverted broken.
key_points: Make it obvious, attractive, easy, satisfying
Invert all four to break bad habits
Plateau of latent potential before breakthrough
how_it_works: Apply four laws to build, invert to break, trust compounding.

title: Habit Stacking
description: Stacking (Clear’s) — the anchored — formulas: the after (the “After [CURRENT HABIT], I will [NEW HABIT]” — the precise), the chained (the multiple — the morning sequence), and the placed (the context — the fitted). The Duhigg pairing (the cue — the existing routine as). The principle: the stacked habit sticks — the anchored precisely, the chained naturally.
how_it_works: Pick anchor habit, write stacking formula, place precisely, chain.

title: Environment Design
description: The environment — the invisible hand — designs: the obvious (the good — the visible; the bad — the hidden), the friction (the good — the reduced; the bad — the increased; the 20-second rule), the cues (the placed — the strategic), and the people (the surrounded — the normal). The choice architecture (the Thaler’s — the nudged). The principle: the designed environment behaves — the good obvious, the bad hard, the normal healthy.
key_points: Join cultures where desired behavior is normal
how_it_works: Audit environment, rearrange cues, adjust friction, choose surroundings.

title: Implementation Intentions
description: Implementation intentions (Gollwitzer’s) — the if-then — plan: the formula (the “If [SITUATION], then I will [BEHAVIOR]” — the precise), the effect (the 2–3x — the follow-through; the researched), and the mechanism (the pre-decided — the automatic). The vs goals (the vague — the beaten). The principle: the if-then’d behavior happens — the pre-decided, the automatic.
how_it_works: Write if-then plans for key behaviors, rehearse mentally, trigger automatically.

title: Habit Tracking Systems
description: Tracking — the measured — systems: the paper (the X’d — the Seinfeld’s “don’t break the chain”), the apps (the Streaks, the Habitica — the gamified), the journal (the BuJo — the gridded), and the reviewed (the weekly — the patterns). The psychology: the visible (the progress — the motivating), and the honest (the missed — the marked). The principle: the tracked habit built — the X’d visibly, the reviewed weekly.
how_it_works: Choose tracker, mark daily, review weekly, resume after misses.

title: Breaking Bad Habits
description: The breaking — the inverted laws — inverts: the invisible (the cue — the removed; the exposure — the reduced), the unattractive (the reframed — the benefits of avoiding), the hard (the friction — the increased; the 20-second), and the unsatisfying (the accountability — the partner; the cost — the immediate). The replacement (the swapped — the routine; the Duhigg’s golden rule). The compassion (the relapsed — the resumed). The principle: the broken habit inverted — the invisible, the hard, the unsatisfying; the replaced kindly.
key_points: Replace routine; resume kindly after relapse
how_it_works: Diagnose loop, invert each law, install replacement, plan relapse response.

title: Identity-Based Habits
description: Identity (Clear’s deepest layer) — the “who” — shifts: the votes (the small wins — the cast for the identity), the proof (the accumulated — the believed), the language (the “I am” — the spoken), and the habits (the aligned — the identity-congruent). The layers: the outcomes (the what), the processes (the how), the identity (the who — the deepest). The principle: the identitied habits stick — the voted daily, the spoken as “I am”.
how_it_works: Choose identity, cast daily votes via small wins, speak it, align habits.

title: The Two-Minute Rule (Habits)
description: The two-minute (Clear’s) — the scaled-down — scales: the mastered (the showing up — the “read before bed” becomes “read one page”), the gateway (the started — the continued naturally), and the standardized (the ritualized — the automatic). The principle: the two-minuted habit started — the scaled to showing up, the gatewayed to more.
how_it_works: Scale habit to 2-min version, do daily, let it grow naturally.

title: Temptation Bundling
description: Bundling (Milkman’s) — the paired — links: the want (the pleasurable — the podcast) with the should (the virtuous — the exercise), the rule (the only — the together), and the enforced (the committed — the gym-only shows). The principle: the bundled temptation motivates — the wanted paired, the only-together ruled.
how_it_works: Identify want and should, link exclusively, enforce the rule.

title: Habit Contracts and Accountability
description: Accountability — the social — contracts: the partner (the check-in — the regular), the stakes (the monetary — the Beeminder; the donated), the public (the committed — the announced), and the coach (the professional — the guided). The principle: the accountable habit kept — the partnered, the staked, the public.
how_it_works: Choose mechanism, set stakes, check in regularly, pay up on failure.

title: The Motivation Myth
description: The myth — the debunked — clarifies: the action (the preceding — the motivation follows), the systems (the relied — the not the feelings), the identity (the driving — the deeper), and the environment (the designed — the automatic). The quote: the “you don’t rise to goals, you fall to systems.” The principle: the systemed behavior persists — the motivation unnecessary, the designed sufficient.
key_points: Fall to systems, not rise to goals
how_it_works: Stop waiting, design systems, act first, let motivation follow.

title: Keystone Habits
description: Keystones (Duhigg’s) — the leveraged — are: the exercise (the classic — the cascading), the making-bed (the correlated — the orderly), the food-journaling (the aware — the cascading), and the identified (the personal — the found). The cascade (the small wins — the spreading). The principle: the keystoned change cascades — the one leveraged, the many shifted.
how_it_works: Identify candidate keystone, install it, watch cascade, reinforce.

title: The 21/66-Day Myth and Reality
description: The timeline — the researched — shows: the 21 (the myth — the Maltz’s misquote), the 66 (the average — the Lally’s 18–254 range), the variable (the complexity — the dependent), and the automaticity (the plateaued — the measured). The implication: the patient (the months — the expected). The principle: the habituated patiently — the 66 expected, the variable accepted.
how_it_works: Commit for 3+ months, track automaticity, persist through plateau.

title: Habit Systems vs Goals
description: The debate — the settled — contrasts: the goals (the direction — the winners and losers share), the systems (the processes — the leading to results), and the integration (the goals set direction — the systems make progress). The Clear: the “forget goals, focus on systems” (the nuanced). The principle: the systemed progress wins — the goals directing, the systems delivering.
how_it_works: Set directional goals, build systems, focus on process daily.

title: Social Habits and Culture
description: The social — the normal — shapes: the tribe (the joined — the desired normal), the expectations (the explicit — the group), and the identity (the shared — the reinforced). The principle: the tribally habituated — the joined where normal is desired, the expected explicitly.
key_points: Join groups where desired behavior is normal
how_it_works: Find tribe with desired norms, join, adopt expectations, reinforce identity.

title: The Habit Audit
description: The audit — the scored — lists: the current (the all — the written), the scored (the +/=/- — the effective, neutral, ineffective), and the redesigned (the kept, the fixed, the dropped). The Clear’s scorecard. The principle: the audited habits redesigned — the scored honestly, the dropped freely.
how_it_works: List habits, score each, redesign: keep, fix, drop.

title: Friction Design in Depth
description: Friction — the 20-second — designs: the good-easy (the guitar — the out; the vitamins — the visible), the bad-hard (the phone — the another room; the snacks — the unstocked), and the measured (the seconds — the counted). The principle: the frictioned behavior shaped — the good easy, the bad hard.
how_it_works: Audit frictions, rearrange: easy for good, hard for bad.

title: Recovery Protocols
description: The recovery — the relapsed — protocols: the never-twice (the rule — the missed once, never twice), the immediate (the resumed — the next opportunity), the examined (the trigger — the learned), and the compassionate (the shame-free — the kind). The principle: the recovered quickly — the never twice, the resumed immediately, the kind always.
how_it_works: Miss once: resume next chance, examine trigger, stay kind.

title: Habit Stacking Sequences
description: The sequences — the chained — build: the morning (the wake — the meditate — the journal — the exercise), the work (the shutdown — the plan — the review), the evening (the dinner — the walk — the read), and the designed (the personal — the fitted). The principle: the sequenced habits flow — the chained naturally, the designed personally.
how_it_works: Map day parts, chain 3–4 habits each, practice sequence.

title: The Compound Effect
description: The compound (Hardy’s) — the multiplied — shows: the small (the daily — the seemingly insignificant), the time (the years — the multiplied), and the choices (the 100% — the owned). The math: the 1% (the 37x — the yearly). The principle: the compounded small wins — the daily owned, the yearly multiplied.
how_it_works: Choose small daily improvements, own them fully, let time multiply.

title: Habit Pairing with Identity
description: The pairing — the deep — links: the habit (the done — the daily), the identity (the reinforced — the “I am a [X]”), and the evidence (the accumulated — the believed). The principle: the paired habit identitied — the done daily, the believed eventually.
how_it_works: Act the habit, speak the identity, accumulate proof, become.

title: Seasonal Habit Resets
description: The resets — the quarterly — refresh: the audited (the scored — the honest), the pruned (the dropped — the freely), the chosen (the 1–2 — the next), and the installed (the designed — the four laws). The principle: the reset seasons grow — the audited quarterly, the chosen few, the installed well.
how_it_works: Audit quarterly, prune, choose 1–2, design and install.

title: The Habit Systems Mastery Path
description: The mastery — the stages — progresses: the installed (the few — the automatic), the stacked (the sequences — the flowing), the identitied (the become — the “I am”), and the teaching (the shared — the multiplied). The principle: the mastered habits lived — the installed, the stacked, the become, the shared.
how_it_works: Install few, stack them, embody identity, teach others.
